title: Champion vs native Ascend aclnn (CANN 9.0.0), measured 2026-11-08

protocol.pypto_side: frozen remote_harness.py, latency_us = median per-round effective_us (PYPTO_BENCH=1)
protocol.aclnn_side: tools/aclnn_bench.py: wall-clock per round (enqueue aclnn + sync), median; executor cached. Both sides end-to-end including host dispatch.
protocol.shape_policy: s-tier {M:512,N:1024} (champion's native c1 contract shape) + m-tier {M:4096,N:4096}; dtype fp32 (champion contract)

results.note: no native rotate-half aclnn op (aclnnRotaryPositionEmbedding is interleaved semantics); baseline is the 6-op elementwise decomposition on contiguous halves. aclnn decomposition is bit-exact vs golden at fp32.
m-tier fp32 is out-of-contract scale-up for this s-tier champion; launches and stays correct but loses to the 6-op aclnn decomposition.

convention: speedup_pypto_vs_aclnn = aclnn_us / pypto_us; >1 means the pypto champion is faster
